level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: Product Analytics and Growth for Builders
audience: Founders and engineers in small teams who own the product numbers: what to measure, how to run experiments and how to grow without a data team.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of metric-design, read-the-query, interpret-the-experiment and pricing questions.
scenarios: Choosing a north-star metric for a new product
Reading an A/B test result correctly
Finding why users churn after week one
Setting a first price and packaging
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Code in fenced blocks with the right language. Question mix: ~30% judgment (which metric, which experiment, which growth loop), ~35% read or debug a SQL query, an event schema or a dashboard, ~35% quantitative interpretation (significance, power, cohorts, funnel and unit economics) with real numbers. Run every SQL example with `node {{root}}/.pipeline/sql/run.mjs <file.sql>` (PostgreSQL 18 via PGlite, pgvector and pg_trgm available). Run every Python example and compute every number with {{root}}/.pipeline/py313/bin/python (CPython 3.13 + PyYAML) or {{root}}/.pipeline/py/bin/python (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn). Compute every statistic (sample sizes, p-values, confidence intervals, lift, retention, LTV, CAC payback) in Python with scipy and state the inputs; prefer worked numbers over formulas alone. Teach statistics correctly: no peeking without sequential methods, multiple-comparison pitfalls, Simpson's paradox, novelty effects. Privacy: consent and GDPR/ePrivacy basics for analytics, cookieless options, data minimisation — cite official regulators (edpb.europa.eu, ico.org.uk, commission.europa.eu). Tools are examples, not endorsements: show PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel or GA4 concepts via their official docs only. Sources: posthog.com/docs, amplitude.com/docs, docs.mixpanel.com, support.google.com/analytics and developers.google.com/analytics, stripe.com/docs and stripe.com/resources, web.dev, w3.org, edpb.europa.eu, ico.org.uk, gdpr-info.eu is NOT allowed (use eur-lex.europa.eu), scipy.org, statsmodels.org, exp-platform/Microsoft Research papers, research.google, arxiv.org, nist.gov; no Medium or growth-hacking blogs.

domains.name: Metrics that matter
skills: North-star and input metrics, metric trees, and avoiding vanity metrics
Activation, engagement, retention and revenue metrics (AARRR) defined precisely for a SaaS or consumer app
Guardrail and counter metrics; Goodhart's law
Leading vs lagging indicators and choosing metric windows
Writing metric definitions people can compute the same way twice

domains.name: Instrumentation and data
skills: Event design: naming conventions, properties, identities, a tracking plan and schema validation
Identity resolution: anonymous to signed-in users, aliasing, cross-device and group (account) analytics
Client vs server-side events, ad blockers, sampling and data loss
Privacy by design: consent, cookieless and first-party analytics, PII minimisation, retention and deletion
Warehouse basics for small teams: Postgres or a warehouse, event tables, idempotent loads

domains.name: Analysis with SQL
skills: Funnels with time windows and step ordering in SQL
Cohort retention curves and tables; unbounded vs bounded retention
Segmentation and the traps: Simpson's paradox, survivorship and selection bias
Window functions for sessions, streaks and time between events
Dashboards that answer questions: one decision per chart, annotations, honest axes

domains.name: Experimentation
skills: A/B test design: hypothesis, unit of randomisation, primary and guardrail metrics, minimum detectable effect
Sample size and power calculations; why small products struggle and what to do instead
Analysis: significance, confidence intervals, peeking, sequential testing and multiple comparisons
Pitfalls: sample ratio mismatch, novelty and primacy effects, interference, bucketing bugs
Feature flags and staged rollouts as experiments; when not to A/B test

domains.name: Growth loops and acquisition
skills: Growth loops vs funnels: viral, content, paid and sales-led loops
Onboarding and time-to-value; activation experiments
SEO and content for developer and B2B products; technical SEO basics
Referral, sharing and network effects; measuring K-factor honestly
Channel economics: CAC by channel, attribution limits and incrementality

domains.name: Pricing and unit economics
skills: Pricing models: per seat, usage-based, tiered, freemium and free trials; packaging and value metrics
Unit economics: gross margin with AI inference costs, LTV, CAC and payback period
Churn types and revenue retention: gross and net revenue retention, expansion
Billing implementation: subscriptions, proration, taxes and merchant of record vs direct
Price changes and testing prices responsibly
